text.insert: In the app, every finished capture goes to the clipboard. A Mac capture of a browser tab can also go to a destination, an OpenCode session on this Mac or on the agent host. This page covers how Annotator picks that session, how a send is retried, and how Paste hands a capture to the app in front. A cabled iPhone and ScrawlKit recordings use the same delivery, as

text.insert: When the topic is unclear, the viewed session never beats the app's own repository, and neither one sends by itself.
A candidate's clue score is the sum, over sources, of the best points that any one clue of that source gives it. Recency is added to that score when it is above zero.
A folder clue gives full points to the sessions closest to its folder, on the line from the project root to the folder or inside it.
A session further along that line loses 15 points for each extra folder, down to half points.
A session elsewhere in the project, or in another checkout of the same repository, gets half points.
A word clue's points are divided by the number of candidates that the word names.
A word names a session through its whole title or its folder's or repository's whole name. It also names a session through a word of a longer title or a piece of its folder's name.
, count only as a whole name.
A piece of a worktree's name counts half. OpenCode's made-up worktree names, such as
Recency gives 20 points within 10 minutes of the capture's end, 12 within an hour, and 5 within a day. It counts the session's update or view times up to a minute after the end.
